subject: Re: Dedicated capacity demo — Aurora.dev (throughput & SLO intake)
messages:
From: Lena Brooks <lena@aurora.dev>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — quick demo request

Hi Sean,

I signed up for Redwood's self-serve last night and we'd like to see a short, technical demo focused on Dedicated capacity for our production footprint. Aurora.dev is evaluating reserved pools because we need predictable throughput and <100ms tail latency for our chat flows.

A few context points:
- Peak concurrent requests: ~220 QPS
- Typical input sequence: 80-120 tokens, responses ~150 tokens
- Batch-friendly workloads (many short requests) but occasional long-form generation

Can someone from sales/solutions walk us through Dedicated (autoscale, model variants, routing/region fallback) and spend 20–30 minutes on sizing guidance? We're based in US-West and would prefer that region for the demo.

Thanks,
Lena Brooks
Head of Platform — Aurora.dev

P.S. Happy to share our traffic sample if helpful (I can attach it after the intro).

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lena Brooks <lena@aurora.dev>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — quick demo request

Hi Lena — great to meet you (virtually) and thanks for signing up. I'm the SDR covering Aurora.dev; Sean is on the thread to loop in Solutions as needed.

We can absolutely run a short, focused session on Dedicated capacity that covers throughput sizing, latency SLO tradeoffs, and fallback policies. Quick ask before we book: can you confirm the ~220 QPS is steady or bursty, and whether the 100ms tail is P95 or P99? That'll help us pick the right demo model configs and whether to show batching and KV cache behavior.

Two slots that work for us (US-West):
- Wed 2027-03-10 10:00–10:30 PT
- Thu 2027-03-11 14:00–14:30 PT

If neither works, share a couple of times and we'll match. I'll attach a short mutual action plan (MAP_Aurora_v1.pdf) with the agenda + pre-demo checklist. Also, if you can upload a small traffic sample (CSV) we'll do a quick back-of-envelope sizing beforehand.

Attachments: MAP_Aurora_v1.pdf

Best,
Ben Carter
SDR, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Ben — thanks. Sorry for not specifying: 220 QPS is our average peak during business hours (burst to ~350 QPS for brief spikes). The 100ms requirement is a P95 target for inference alone. We can share a sample CSV (I've attached a 24h sample below) and our internal SLO doc.

The Thu 2027-03-11 14:00 PT slot works best for us — please book that if it's still open.

Attachments: Aurora_Traffic_Sample.csv, aurora_slo_v1.pdf

Looking forward to the demo agenda in the MAP.

— Lena

Thanks for the sample and SLO, Lena — that was helpful. Thu 2027-03-11 14:00 PT is booked on our end. Monica (Solutions Engineer) will run the demo and cover autoscale policies, model variant fallbacks, and network/region considerations specific to US-West.

Quick pre-demo checklist (attached in MAP):
- Confirm test account & preferred model type (gpt-4-style or instruction-tuned open model)
- Provide a short traffic sample (we have your CSV) and a note on acceptable tokenization split
- Any non-functional requirements (encryption at rest, audit logs)

Attachment: SLO-checklist.xlsx (internal checklist we use to validate demo scope)
